feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
entry.summary:
Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) enhances diffusion distillation by combining reverse-KL score matching with explicit moment constraints on feature means and standard deviations computed from the generator's EMA copy.

Why it matters: IDM achieves state-of-the-art text rendering performance on LongText-Bench at two network function evaluations without requiring auxiliary external encoders.

entry.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
A-RSI enables zero-data multimodal self-improvement by using training dynamics to adaptively refresh a pool of programmatically generated tasks without external data or test-set access.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that vision-language models can continuously self-improve without human labels, external datasets, or validation leakages by algorithmically managing their own task refresh cycles.

entry.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
entry.summary:
LOWN is a training-free decoding method for Diffusion Vision-Language Models that reduces FLOPs by skipping visual token processing whenever image-free predictions match previous image-conditioned outputs.

Why it matters: It drastically cuts inference computational overhead in diffusion VLMs without requiring model retraining, fine-tuning, or performance tradeoffs.

entry.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
entry.summary:
L3G-World enables real-time 9 FPS infinite world generation using a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory that updates with scene extent rather than stream length.

Why it matters: By removing VAE re-encoding bottlenecks and decoupling memory growth from stream length, the architecture achieves 9 FPS real-time generation of spatially consistent, long-horizon interactive 3D environments.

entry.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
entry.summary:
WorkFactory is a scalable framework that uses information support graphs and probe executions to construct 112,686 executable professional tasks across 612 occupations for training working agents.

Why it matters: It provides an automated methodology to fix defective task environments and generate massive, reliable demonstration datasets for training AI agents on complex real-world occupations.

entry.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
entry.summary:
SpecSlot is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples spectral detail from global attention sequence length by expanding spatial anchors into frequency-specific slots that interact locally.

Why it matters: It enables generative Transformers to scale up fine-grained spatial and spectral visual details without incurring the quadratic computational costs of long global attention sequences.

entry.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
entry.summary:
Co-Design Bench is a reference-free benchmark containing 273 multimodal tasks and 2,331 hidden criteria to evaluate agentic models on real-user application editing.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, execution-based standard for evaluating how effectively AI agents convert complex multimodal user feedback into fully functional codebases.

entry.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
entry.summary:
HairDeck is a set diffusion transformer that generates animation-ready stylized hair cards and spring-bone chains from a single image.

Why it matters: It enables rapid creation of fully animatable stylized 3D character hair assets from a single input image for games and avatars.

entry.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
entry.summary:
WeVisCut introduces a 9B single-agent policy and harness for long-form script-to-video editing that matches Claude Opus 5 performance while using 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute.

Why it matters: It proves that a compact, task-adapted 9B model can achieve frontier-level video editing quality at a fraction of the computational and token cost of large generalist LLMs.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
entry.summary:
IntReal introduces IntReal-100K, a real-world multimodal interleaved dataset, along with a fine-grained, seven-dimension evaluation suite that achieves strong human agreement and low redundancy for benchmarking Unified Multimodal Models.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark for interleaved generation and demonstrates that models can be improved via modality-specific optimization rather than relying strictly on joint text-image training.

entry.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions
entry.summary:
PhysInsert is a framework for physically plausible object insertion that utilizes VGGT geometry streams and 2D spatial supervision to jointly adapt object pose, illumination, and scene interactions using a novel Blender-rendered dataset.

Why it matters: It enables more realistic synthetic image editing and composition by ensuring inserted objects automatically match the perspective, pose, and lighting of the target environment.

entry.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
entry.summary:
WebAnything is a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable web environments from real URLs using an Explorer-Builder and an independent verifier, eliminating per-site manual setup and repairs.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, reproducible training and evaluation of web agents by automatically converting real-world websites into executable environments without manual engineering.

entry.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
entry.summary:
Glance unifies reranking and generation into a single resident 9B model using a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to score candidate passages from a shared prefill.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to host and run separate models for reranking and generation in RAG pipelines, significantly reducing latency, GPU memory overhead, and redundant processing.

entry.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
AskStream is a streaming video benchmark introducing an 'ask' action to help multimodal models actively request missing information under video or user uncertainty.

Why it matters: It establishes a standard for evaluating proactive agents that must clarify ambiguous user queries or incomplete video inputs instead of waiting indefinitely or hallucinating responses.

entry.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
entry.summary:
EditAgent improves agentic image editing by expanding the action space with specialized tools and enhancing the observation space with structured verification records for parallel listwise judging.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining specialized tool routing with parallel candidate verification significantly cuts compute costs and improves quality over traditional sequential refinement in vision-language tasks.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
entry.summary:
Researchers debunk the Neural Thickets weight-geometry hypothesis, demonstrating that its gains stem from output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting, which can be matched using a training-free logit perturbation method called PSV.

Why it matters: Logit PSV provides a simple, computation-light, training-free alternative to weight-perturbation ensembles across language and vision models without requiring model weight modifications.

entry.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
SCARL reshapes reinforcement learning advantages using sequence-confidence alignment gaps, preventing entropy collapse and improving language-model reasoning without requiring extra forward/backward passes.

Why it matters: SCARL enhances policy optimization in verifiable reasoning tasks by preventing premature entropy collapse and better separating correct from incorrect responses across diverse RL estimators.

entry.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
entry.summary:
A comprehensive study on dense decoder-only transformers reveals that looping strategies must align with parameter or training FLOP constraints, and introduces adapter specialization and modified parallel looping to improve quality and inference speed.

Why it matters: Designing looped transformers according to specific compute constraints and architecture modifications allows practitioners to scale model depth and inference throughput without increasing parameter counts.

entry.title: Distributional Reward Calibration and Budget-Neutral Credit Assignment for Multimodal RLVR
entry.summary:
TACE improves GRPO advantage estimation through optimal-transport reward standardization and budget-neutral token credit assignment.

Why it matters: TACE prevents heavy-tailed reward outliers and unconstrained token updates from destabilizing reinforcement learning from verifier rewards (RLVR) in multimodal models.

entry.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
Exponential residual flows (ERFs) introduce a deterministic, ODE-based sampling framework for discrete diffusion models by augmenting discrete tokens with continuous residual variables.

Why it matters: It enables deterministic probability flow sampling and consistency distillation in discrete diffusion models, leading to faster sampling and improved performance in text and code generation.

entry.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
entry.summary:
A unified framework replaces the multi-stage training pipeline by deriving RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, training foundation models with a single likelihood-based algorithm.

Why it matters: It simplifies the foundation model post-training infrastructure and improves compute efficiency by replacing disparate training algorithms with a single likelihood-based system.

entry.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
entry.summary:
Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP) prevents model degradation during sequential LLM unlearning by restricting gradient updates to the orthogonal complement of low-rank activation subspaces cached from previous forget sets.

Why it matters: COP enables long-term compliance with data removal requests (such as privacy or copyright enforcement) in deployed LLMs without causing performance collapse or requiring costly retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Latent Path Exploration via Potential-Guided Subtrajectory Balance
entry.summary:
SubLAT improves stochastic continuous latent reasoning in language models by coupling a relative answer potential with Subtrajectory Balance to guide intermediate transition paths.

Why it matters: It enables language models to effectively explore complex, multi-path reasoning spaces in continuous latent representations without producing explicit token traces.

entry.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
entry.summary:
The CATT benchmark isolates LM data attribution failures, revealing that negative log-odds gradients and top-token aggregation significantly improve attribution recall over standard document-averaging cross-entropy methods.

Why it matters: Simple changes to loss gradient formulation and token aggregation can dramatically improve the accuracy of tracing specific outputs back to training data without inventing new estimators.

entry.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation
entry.summary:
Multi-View MoE uses multiple independent routers to aggregate expert scores and dynamically mix latent input views for expert computation without increasing the active-expert budget.

Why it matters: It improves MoE routing accuracy and downstream performance at zero additional FLOP or communication cost per active expert.

entry.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO) combines Multiscale Advantage Estimation and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the assistant-turn scale for long-horizon LLM agents.

Why it matters: It provides a more accurate credit assignment mechanism for reinforcement learning, improving the execution of multi-step, long-horizon tasks by LLM agents.

entry.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Denoising Token Credit Assignment (DTCA) improves reinforcement learning for diffusion language models by assigning token-level rewards based on prediction confidence gains, POS grouping, and entropy changes.

Why it matters: DTCA solves the credit assignment problem in iterative diffusion language models, significantly boosting mathematical reasoning performance without relying solely on sparse outcome rewards.

entry.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RealSSA, a realistic streaming audio-visual speaker extraction benchmark, alongside Falcon, an efficient single-pass causal separation model trained with an encoder-space contrastive loss.

Why it matters: Falcon enables high-quality, real-time target speaker extraction on edge devices by significantly reducing memory, computational, and latency overhead in complex acoustic environments.

entry.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
entry.summary:
OmniShowcase improves subject-consistent 360-degree video generation by combining a 3D-asset-based synthetic data pipeline with geometry conditioning via reference-derived surface-normal turntables.

Why it matters: Explicit 3D surface-normal conditioning resolves subject identity loss and geometry breakdown during extreme viewpoint shifts like 360-degree camera orbits.

entry.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
entry.summary:
Sensorimotor Alignment (S^2) is a training-free offline metric that evaluates robot foundation models by measuring how well their sensory representations align with the geometry of physical motion.

Why it matters: It enables researchers to prioritize and screen robot foundation models and VLM backbones off-line before spending resources on expensive fine-tuning and physical closed-loop evaluations.

entry.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
entry.summary:
EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model supporting text, image, audio, and video inputs within a single unified representation space, outperforming models up to twelve times larger.

Why it matters: It establishes a new Pareto frontier in multimodal embedding efficiency, delivering state-of-the-art cross-modal representation quality in resource-constrained environments.

entry.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
entry.summary:
The h1 harness demonstrates that a simple agentic loop scaling test-time compute via verifier feedback outperforms specialized formal theorem proving workflows when paired with an efficient Lean 4 interface.

Why it matters: It suggests that automated theorem proving gains come more from scaling test-time compute through efficient environment feedback than from complex, human-designed orchestration workflows.

entry.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
entry.summary:
TAO is a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM agent serving that optimizes session admission and GPU placement using dynamic programming based on tool readiness, time-decayed cache credit, and token footprints.

Why it matters: By accounting for external tool execution states and KV cache locality, TAO significantly reduces serving latency and boosts throughput for complex, multi-turn LLM agent workloads.

entry.title: Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models
entry.summary:
Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD) uses second-order image statistics and trainable coefficient interfaces to accelerate training and improve generation quality in pixel-space flow models without modifying native decoder blocks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that incorporating frozen or statistically initialized denoisers into the decoder structure significantly reduces the computational burden and epoch count required to train pixel-space diffusion and flow models.

entry.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
entry.summary:
RynnWorld-Latent is a cross-embodiment video world model that conditions video transformers on 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on heterogeneous human and robot interaction videos.

Why it matters: It enables scalable world-model pretraining on mass human and diverse robot video data, boosting synthetic data quality and downstream policy success rates on benchmarks like LIBERO and real-world platforms.

entry.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Unigram Cross-Entropy (UCE), a model-free, tokenizer-agnostic metric that measures corpus-benchmark lexical alignment and consistently tracks zero-shot accuracy across model scales.

Why it matters: UCE enables predictable data curation and targeted prompt routing by quantifying how pre-training data distributions directly dictate zero-shot model performance.

entry.title: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
entry.summary:
OSMA-Bench evaluates obstacle-conditioned safe motion adaptation in household robot navigation using spatially matched scenarios and the new Semantic Sensitivity Index (SSI) to measure whether motion parameters reflect obstacle safety semantics.

Why it matters: Current robot navigation policies suffer from a semantic-to-motion grounding gap, recognizing obstacle safety risks without translating that awareness into safer physical movement.

entry.title: Timestral
entry.summary:
Timestral is a new family of four probabilistic time series foundation models (5M to 209M parameters) that achieves state-of-the-art results across major forecasting benchmarks.

Why it matters: Timestral establishes a new state of the art in probabilistic time series forecasting using fully open-sourced models and code.

entry.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
entry.summary:
A theoretical and empirical study revealing that post-trained agent policies implicitly encode harness-specific preferences, causing performance to drop significantly when harnesses change even if task-optimal decisions remain identical.

Why it matters: Evaluating or changing agent interfaces with fixed models is misleading; maximizing performance requires re-training policies under the new harness to leverage higher harness ceilings.

entry.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced CrossProfile, a 480-task diagnostic benchmark showing that common LLM memory compression heuristics (relevance and rarity filtering) systematically fail in multi-agent group decision-making.

Why it matters: Naively summarising multi-agent discussions or relying on full transcripts actively degrades downstream decision accuracy due to systemic heuristics failures and agent-attribution biases.

entry.title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
entry.summary:
A new framework optimizes LLM agent scaffold evolution by combining sparse search-time feedback with paired successive halving for final confirmation, matching or exceeding full-evaluation performance using roughly 50% fewer execution cells.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the high computational execution costs of developing LLM agent scaffolds without sacrificing final model quality.

entry.title: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
entry.summary:
LinMix frames data mixing as a linear domain attribution problem, replacing Dirichlet sampling with vertex sampling on the capped simplex to enable scalable, linear domain selection.

Why it matters: LinMix eliminates the need for expensive proxy model search heuristics, enabling efficient and mathematically optimal pretraining data mixture optimization across hundreds of fine-grained domains.

entry.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
entry.summary:
EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model that unifies text, image, audio, and video representations using simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum.

Why it matters: It establishes a new efficiency and performance Pareto frontier for multimodal embeddings, enabling scalable multi-modal retrieval and representation on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
entry.summary:
A theoretical and empirical study shows that KL-regularized agent post-training embeds the decision preferences of the training harness into the policy, making evaluation across different harnesses with a fixed model misleading.

Why it matters: Evaluating agent harnesses using a static model misleads developer choices because harness changes alter performance ceilings that require further post-training to realize.

entry.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
entry.summary:
MERLIN enhances Multi-State Linear Attention by tracking key moments to compute both the mean and variance of query-segment alignments for improved memory routing.

Why it matters: MERLIN provides an efficient, low-overhead routing mechanism that significantly boosts the long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities of linear-time state-space and attention models.

entry.title: What Survives Distillation? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2
entry.summary:
Mechanistic evaluation of DistilGPT-2 reveals a circuit-dependent dichotomy where the Indirect Object Identification circuit collapses entirely while the Greater-Than circuit survives distillation via active head remapping.

Why it matters: Aggregate performance metrics mask internal circuit failures, proving that mechanistic interpretability is essential to verify if distilled models actually retain complex reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Mechanistic Failure Modes of Weight Pruning in Transformer Language Models
entry.summary:
Mechanistic evaluation of pruned GPT-2 models reveals that magnitude neuron pruning causes circuit inversion, where output accuracy drops dramatically despite low perplexity and intact attention heads.

Why it matters: Standard evaluation metrics like perplexity and structural integrity checks fail to detect critical internal circuit damage, necessitating circuit-level causal analysis when evaluating compressed language models.

entry.title: Self-Regularized Flow Language Models
entry.summary:
SERF is a self-supervised framework for continuous flow language models that uses noisy-to-clean self-distillation via an EMA teacher to accelerate training and improve generation quality without external models or inference changes.

Why it matters: SERF substantially speeds up training and enables drastically faster, few-step generation in continuous diffusion language models without altering the inference procedure.

entry.title: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
HiLo-RD is a cross-budget self-distillation method that aligns small-window hidden representations with large-window teacher states in masked diffusion language models to prevent premature commitment.

Why it matters: It enables masked diffusion language models to achieve higher accuracy and more concise outputs under strict computational generation budgets using self-supervision.

entry.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
entry.summary:
Researchers prove that under per-entity frame freedom, relation updates mathematically require gauge-equivariant Wilson loops, establishing holonomy attention as the unique symmetric edge attention mechanism for relational graphs.

Why it matters: It establishes a mathematically non-negotiable architecture for non-abelian relation composition, enabling robust graph reasoning and anomaly detection on noisy relational data without training.

entry.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
entry.summary:
ChronoReplay addresses interface lock-in in streaming spatial VLMs by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes with source-native targets and balanced family weighting.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how to train a single spatial VLM checkpoint that excels across diverse spatial tasks without sacrificing performance on unaligned spatial readouts.

entry.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
The Trinity is a recursive self-improvement framework that couples world generation with Harness evolution using Creator, Explorer, and Evolver roles to optimize multimodal agents via a capability tree.

Why it matters: It automates environment creation and agent harness iteration, removing key bottlenecks in scaling multimodal and embodied AI self-improvement.

entry.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
entry.summary:
PDRVLA integrates a lightweight Physical Dynamics Module to condition action generation on future RGB, depth, and optical-flow feature predictions without video generation latency.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that VLA models can leverage world-model physical dynamics representations to improve robotic manipulation performance without incurring the computational latency of video generation.

entry.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
entry.summary:
Hy-Nomas is an 8B diffusion video world model designed for multi-turn, free-form text and camera-controlled interactive world generation using cached history and action-aware causal attention.

Why it matters: It advances multi-turn interactive video generation by establishing a framework that maintains historical consistency while accurately processing dynamic, instruction-driven actions.

entry.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
entry.summary:
A large-scale evaluation reveals dedicated agent memory systems often underperform naive RAG, introducing a framework that balances memory benefits against the performance degradation caused by memory tax.

Why it matters: It shifts AI agent development toward measuring net value against naive retrieval, preventing engineers from deploying complex memory systems that inadvertently degrade task performance.

entry.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
entry.summary:
Researchers show discrete visual tokens can match continuous representations in multimodal understanding using Factorized Vector Quantization (FVQ) to scale effective bit budgets without semantic saturation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that discrete visual representations can achieve parity with continuous ones, enabling fully unified next-token prediction architectures for large-scale native multimodal models.

entry.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
entry.summary:
VibeVideoBench is a benchmark of 239 tasks evaluating multimodal agents on code-driven video generation without using external image or video diffusion models.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark demonstrating that multimodal agents can generate precise, rule-consistent, synchronized video content purely through code generation and execution.

entry.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
entry.summary:
Rollback turns action-conditioned world models into counterfactual engines by rewinding to decision points, generating fine-grained action-level supervision without a separate value model.

Why it matters: It enables rapid real-world robotic policy improvement by leveraging counterfactual imagination in world models alongside dynamic online dynamics correction.

entry.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
entry.summary:
Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME) replaces test-time weight updates with external memory distillation for scientific discovery, outperforming test-time training while significantly reducing computational overhead.

Why it matters: TTME provides a far more computationally efficient test-time adaptation method for open-weight LLMs without sacrificing performance on scientific discovery tasks.

entry.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
entry.summary:
CodeCap-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on generating executable code as video captions, demonstrating that code representations outperform natural language in downstream video QA and reconstruction tasks.

Why it matters: Using executable code as a video captioning format provides a precise, unambiguous representation that improves downstream video reasoning and visual reconstruction fidelity.

entry.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
entry.summary:
ThinkWorld is a Vision-Language-Action framework that represents action reasoning via discrete Chain-of-Dynamics motion tokens and uses reinforcement learning on video state transitions to bridge human and robot data.

Why it matters: It allows robotic systems to leverage vast, unannotated human video datasets for action reasoning, improving transfer learning and generalization to unseen environments.

entry.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
entry.summary:
LociArt introduces a unified paradigm and the GRNStyle model for free-style local video stylization, allowing precise multi-region artistic editing while preserving non-target video content.

Why it matters: It enables fine-grained, multi-style spatial video editing without compromising temporal consistency or damaging unedited visual regions.

entry.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
entry.summary:
SPOT introduces a lightweight 0.62M-parameter order-prediction model and coupled-noise matching to enable lossless speculative decoding for diffusion language models, accelerating target throughput by up to 3.4 times.

Why it matters: It removes the trade-off between speed and output quality in diffusion language models by making lossless multi-token speculative decoding feasible and highly efficient.

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
entry.summary:
Zooming without Zooming v2 uses EvidenceConnect, a data synthesis framework using zoomed-in image regions and RLVR, to improve multimodal perception without task-specific training data.

Why it matters: It enables generalizable multimodal perception and spatial reasoning across downstream agent and long-context benchmarks using synthetic data rather than costly task-specific datasets.

entry.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
entry.summary:
A new channel selection method uses top-k selection instead of offline-calibrated thresholds to achieve data-free, constant-budget MoE decoding speedups while avoiding repetition collapse.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for offline calibration datasets while delivering robust, deterministic memory read reductions and faster MoE inference speeds without degrading model accuracy.

entry.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
entry.summary:
MuonGS introduces Gram-Schmidt projection into the Muon optimizer to remove radial update components, relaxing weight-norm constraints to enable faster accumulated effective learning rate growth and improved LLM pretraining performance.

Why it matters: Relaxing strict weight-norm constraints allows optimizers to sustain exploration late in training, providing up to a 15% token efficiency gain over state-of-the-art Muon variants.

entry.title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
entry.summary:
The paper introduces the "structure gap," proving mathematically and empirically that finite data cannot match the finite-resource accuracy, extrapolation, and certification of methods incorporating known domain structure.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling dataset size alone cannot replace explicit domain constraints for certified generalization and extrapolation in structured tasks.

entry.title: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce parameterized steering to set activations to precise trait strengths and vector orthogonalization to enable interference-free, multi-attribute LLM activation steering.

Why it matters: These techniques allow fine-grained, independent control over multiple model behaviors at inference time without requiring retraining or incurring trait interference.

entry.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
entry.summary:
SimpleLoRIF scales gradient attribution to million-example datasets by restricting backpropagation to final transformer blocks, enabling the identification and filtering of benign-looking fine-tuning data that erodes LLM safety.

Why it matters: It enables practical, large-scale dataset filtering of seemingly benign training data that causes safety degradation without relying on LLM-as-a-judge models or sacrificing model capability.

entry.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
entry.summary:
PerceptRL enhances MLLM visual perception post-training using single-turn Perception RL on auto-generated QA pairs alongside multi-turn Perception Agentic RL with grounding-aware tool rewards and coordinate injection.

Why it matters: It establishes a verifiable reinforcement learning framework that prevents the decay of fine-grained visual perception during post-training while mitigating coordinate drift in multi-turn tool-using MLLMs.

entry.title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training
entry.summary:
AdaRoll-GRPO models rollout allocation as a Bayes-adaptive MDP to dynamically distribute rollout budgets based on question difficulty during LLM post-training.

Why it matters: It improves LLM training efficiency and reasoning performance under constrained computational budgets without adding runtime overhead.

entry.title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
entry.summary:
CauTrace is a white-box diagnostic framework that identifies why LLMs fail by tracking functional states, representation propagation, temporal-state coordination, and reasoning trajectory dynamics.

Why it matters: It unifies the diagnosis of ordinary and adversarially induced LLM failures by examining internal mechanism dynamics rather than just evaluating final output correctness.

entry.title: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR
entry.summary:
Researchers show that policy collapse in label-free RLVR is a collective instability driven by cross-task coupling, predicting and proving a critical dataset size threshold N_c beyond which shared parameter perturbations outpace per-problem sharpening.

Why it matters: Understanding cross-task coupling enables the design of mitigation strategies—such as removing shared gradient directions or adding marginal-entropy bonuses—to prevent performance collapse in label-free RLVR.

entry.title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation on MoHoBench reveals how inference-time instructions, post-training, and internal activation interventions jointly manipulate refusal behavior on visually unanswerable questions across three MLLMs.

Why it matters: Evaluating safety and reliability in MLLMs requires disentangling actual visual evidence recognition from a model's general propensity to refuse.

entry.title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
entry.summary:
WM-Basin is a black-box detector that identifies distilled LLMs by detecting a persistent, key-specific geometric signal left in the parameter space by watermarked teacher traces.

Why it matters: It provides model providers with a robust method to prove unauthorized API-based distillation of their proprietary models, even when students sample at low temperatures or apply post-processing.

entry.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
entry.summary:
Trajectory2Gym synthesizes tool-use agent supervision by constructing executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and filtering for actions grounded in the agent's visible interaction history.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling tool-use agents requires constructing learnable, decision-grounded interaction environments rather than merely collecting successful raw trajectories.

entry.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
entry.summary:
StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and hierarchical memory harness designed to infer implicit, dynamic user intents and improve proactive video interactions.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language models to proactively assist users during real-time tasks without requiring continuous explicit prompts or losing track of changing context.

entry.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
entry.summary:
DynaFlow introduces free-form executable workflow synthesis into a main agent's action space, enabling dynamically generated, code-based multi-agent orchestration without fine-tuning sub-agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training a single agent to dynamically write program-based orchestration flows significantly outperforms static multi-agent architectures without needing to retrain underlying sub-agent executors.

entry.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
entry.summary:
InteractiveWorld is the first verifiable environment for closed-loop human-AI interaction, featuring InteractiveBench to evaluate MLLM assistants across 120 multi-turn tasks using state-based rewards.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, reproducible platform to test and advance egocentric MLLMs for real-world physical assistance without relying on costly human trials.

entry.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
entry.summary:
This paper presents a system-level framework for work agents, defining execution across stateful workspaces, task classifications, core capability families, and optimization strategies for models and runtime harnesses.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified framework for designing, optimizing, and evaluating AI agents to reliably execute complex, verifiable work in real-world digital environments.

entry.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
entry.summary:
AMBIT is a unified framework for First-Order Ambisonics generation and editing using a shared Transfusion backbone, an FOA-aware continuous VAE, and joint on-policy self-distillation.

Why it matters: It improves source preservation and spatial quality in native FOA audio editing and generation, allowing precise instruction-guided manipulation of 3D soundscapes.

entry.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
entry.summary:
Principia is an LLM-based framework that constructs, applies, and continually refines task-specific comparative causal hypotheses and inductive scientific principles directly at test time using ongoing observations.

Why it matters: It automates the labor-intensive hypotheses-to-principle translation stage, allowing language models to continuously evolve scientific domain knowledge directly during inference across complex discovery benchmarks.

entry.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
entry.summary:
Δτ-Bench is an executable agent benchmark containing 1,588 multi-turn tasks across 42 domains designed to evaluate LLM agent adaptation to evolving tool ecosystems.

Why it matters: It exposes the fragility of current LLM agents and skill-learning techniques when operating in real-world software environments with constantly changing API tools.

entry.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
entry.summary:
Qwen-Image-PE enhances text-to-image prompts using a two-stage training strategy with Caption-Based Reverse Distillation and Groupwise Design Reward to improve fine-grained visual design.

Why it matters: It establishes an open-weights method for prompt expansion that systematically optimizes specific design dimensions and generalizes across diverse downstream text-to-image models.

entry.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
entry.summary:
This survey provides an operational definition and process framework for trustworthy recursive self-improvement (RSI) in large models, categorizing requirements across four interconnected themes and three evaluative perspectives.

Why it matters: As large models autonomously modify their own prompts, tools, and update mechanisms, structured frameworks for trustworthy RSI are necessary to prevent catastrophic alignment failure, capability degradation, and lost human oversight.

entry.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
entry.summary:
AV-FABLE is a new dual-timeline benchmark containing 998 hours of long-form audio-visual videos designed to evaluate localized, sparse AI manipulations across independent audio and visual timelines.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard language outputs from AV-LLMs fail to report deepfakes despite encoding the necessary forensic features, providing a framework to extract accurate multimodal temporal localization.

entry.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary:
HiP3R introduces a training-free hierarchical pose graph that resolves camera drift and coordinate inconsistency in long-horizon 3D reconstruction from feed-forward models.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, globally consistent 3D reconstruction and accurate camera trajectory estimation for long video sequences containing thousands of frames without retraining existing models.

entry.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
S3AC introduces a critic-training recipe and Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling for LLM reasoning, outperforming critic-free methods across models up to 397B parameters.

Why it matters: It enables stable actor-critic reinforcement learning for long chain-of-thought reasoning, avoiding the rollout waste and performance degradation of critic-free baseline approaches.

entry.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
entry.summary:
EmbodiedLab is a benchmark containing 30 physics-simulated science experiments designed to evaluate embodied agents on tasks where physical manipulation is required to acquire unknown scientific knowledge.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between traditional manipulation benchmarks and scientific discovery benchmarks by requiring agents to execute physical experimentation to discover dynamic parameters.

entry.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
entry.summary:
RynnVLA-Latent enables cross-embodiment robot pretraining by extracting 3D-grounded continuous latent actions from unlabeled videos, bypassing the need for native action labels.

Why it matters: It removes the bottleneck of scarce action-labeled robot datasets by allowing policies to pretrain on abundant, heterogeneous human and simulation videos.

entry.title: CANS: Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering (CANS) is a training-free framework that uses closed-form neuron-wise scaling coefficients to dynamically control LLM behavior while preserving general model capabilities.

Why it matters: CANS provides an efficient, training-free method to safely steer model behaviors without incurring inference-time latency or significantly degrading general capabilities.

entry.title: Test-Time Confidence Adaptation under RL-Induced Trajectory Shift
entry.summary:
StaR-TTA enables test-time confidence adaptation for post-reinforcement-learning LLMs by exploiting a preserved relationship where stable reasoning trajectories remain more likely to yield correct answers without target labels.

Why it matters: It provides a label-free method to maintain reliable confidence estimates for LLM reasoning outputs after the models undergo trajectory-shifting reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
entry.summary:
Skill$^{\infty}$ introduces a recursive self-improvement framework where a meta-agent uses a task-decoupled meta-skill to optimize task skills, while recursively optimizing the meta-skill using the exact same procedure.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical mechanism for recursive self-improvement by enabling language agents to autonomously optimize both task-level procedural knowledge and the meta-level procedures used to refine that knowledge.

entry.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
entry.summary:
FOCUS is an agentic reinforcement learning method that uses selective branching and active critic learning to improve value estimation and credit assignment in long-horizon language model tasks.

Why it matters: FOCUS solves the credit assignment problem in long-horizon LLM tasks by efficiently targeting compute toward uncertain state value estimates rather than using uniform, high-cost continuation sampling.

entry.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Selective Tie Learning, a method using implicit reward margins and curvature approximations to select optimal tie data for reducing spurious correlations in preference optimization.

Why it matters: It enables more data-efficient preference tuning of language models by strategically selecting tie samples to eliminate shortcut learning without uniform dataset expansion.

entry.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
S3AC introduces a practical critic-training recipe alongside Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling to enable stable token-level credit assignment and prompt selection for LLM chain-of-thought reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that stabilized critic-based actor-critic methods can outperform critic-free baseline approaches like GRPO in large-scale LLM reasoning tasks while maintaining single-rollout efficiency.

entry.title: GPDPO: Learning from Reward Conflicts via Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization (GPDPO) resolves multi-reward conflicts in LLM alignment by extracting auxiliary pairwise preference signals from Pareto-dominance relations in conflict-filtered rollouts.

Why it matters: GPDPO maximizes sample efficiency in multi-reward LLM alignment by converting otherwise discarded conflicting rollouts into useful preference supervision.

entry.title: Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE) on Rare-Failure Rates of Fine-Tuned LLMs
entry.summary:
Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE) is a method that efficiently estimates rare safety-fine-tuning failure probabilities by amplifying failure rates via token log-probability changes and extrapolating back using a score-function estimator.

Why it matters: ALE enables accurate measurement of extremely rare LLM safety failures without incurring the prohibitive computational cost of direct sampling.

entry.title: LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
LoopFold accelerates looped Transformers by using a lightweight predictor and corrector to compute multiple recurrent depths in parallel for the same token prefix, reducing decoding latency.

Why it matters: It enables deeper, more accurate looped Transformer architectures to overcome sequential recurrent depth bottlenecks and achieve lower inference latency.

entry.title: StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
StateLoop introduces a persistent, token-wise state with learned gating to improve parameter-efficient looped Transformers by carrying information across deep iterations.

Why it matters: StateLoop enhances the performance and capability of parameter-efficient looped Transformers without requiring deeper parameter footprints as recurrent depth grows.
